title: Spot the leak and the bias
goal: Catch a prompt that leaks student data and an output that carries bias — de-identify before you send.

blocks.title: Two risks, hiding together
blocks.body:
Every time you use AI, two risks sit side by side.

One is what you put in — a prompt can quietly leak a child's private details. The other is what it gives back — the output can carry bias you didn't ask for.

Catching both, before you use anything, is the skill this lesson builds.

blocks.template: Same need, safe prompt. De-identify it: "Suggest a gentle support plan for {{who}} who {{detail}}."

options: was diagnosed with dyslexia and lives with her grandmother

blocks.question: You ask AI for 10 example word problems about jobs. Every doctor and engineer in the list is a boy; every nurse and cook is a girl. What's going on?

options.text: Bias — it's stereotyping jobs by gender; ask it to mix the roles
Nothing — that's just how the examples came out
A factual error in the maths

blocks.explanation: Caught it. 👏 AI learns from patterns in old text, so it can quietly repeat stereotypes — by gender, region, caste or religion. Noticing it and asking for balance keeps your classroom fair. That eye is yours, not the tool's.

blocks.question: How ready do you feel to catch a data leak and a biased output before you use them?
